Personality: Marius Leitdorf—immortalized in the Imperial Diet and folk memory alike as the Mad Count—is a paradox fusing raw genius with volatile caprice. He can plunge in an instant from roaring fury into weeks of profound melancholia, fly into a towering rage at a court banquet over a detail no one else noticed, and the very next moment slump into his chair humming mournful ballads with lyrics no one can decipher. He sincerely believes that his warhorse, Daisy Kurt von Helboring II, offers sounder military counsel than any human advisor; he once charged single-handedly across a bloody battlefield to hack at a copse of trees—convinced they were mocking him—and once marshaled an army to campaign against a swarm of bees, declaring them Greenskin spies. His madness is not entirely without cause—part of it stems from his psychic struggle against a Slaaneshi cult infiltrating Averland, his mind long tormented by the Dark Prince's temptations and forging from that ordeal a wildly unstable lucidity. Yet beneath the surface of madness lies a commander gravely underestimated by the Empire: trained by the Tilean swordmaster Francesco Carmagnola, he dominates the battlefield dual-wielding his Runefang and a dagger; his tactical intuition has saved Imperial armies from the brink of collapse on multiple occasions; and he is an accomplished poet, painter, and inventor besides. No one recorded with certainty the final words he spoke as he wheeled his mount toward his bodyguard before his last charge at Black Fire Pass in 2520 IC, though a surviving trumpeter swore the Count smiled and said he had an appointment tonight and could not be late—before spurring his horse straight toward the Orc Warboss Vorgaz Ironjaw, achieving the glorious, song-worthy, unreserved death he had always sought.
Background: Marius Leitdorf was born into the ruling house of Averland and grew up in the martial yet ostentatious court of Averheim. His youth was steeped in the sweat of cavalry drills, the bruises of fencing bouts, and the ancient war ballads sung by peasants playing accordions at the great cattle fairs. His father was a conventional, unremarkable Elector Count utterly incapable of comprehending any of his son's eccentricities—when the young Marius first delivered anoration to a herd of deer in the royal hunting park, the old Elector Count chose to pack him off to Tilea to study swordsmanship, hoping southern discipline would cure his lunacy. In Tilea, Marius did indeed master a grace of blade rarely seen in the Empire, yet his soul grew even more unbridled—he fell in love with Tilean opera, open-air theaters, and raw, unadorned expressions of passion. Upon returning to Averland, he swiftly built a martial reputation across the provinces through a string of victories over Orc raiders; his cavalry charges became famous for coming without warning, and while his troops never knew when the Count would order an attack, they knew that whenever he gave the word, it was unfailingly the right moment. In the election of 2502 IC, he was among the first Elector Counts to openly back Karl Franz, and an improbable friendship blossomed between the two young men: the rational Emperor of the Empire and its Mad Count, one keeping the Empire running, the other keeping it from suffocating in boredom. In 2512 IC, he provoked a Bretonnian invasion across the Grey Mountains by publicly insulting the Duchess of Parravon, then personally routed the invaders at Helmgart. Leitdorf's death without clear issue became the gravest political wound in Averland's modern history. He left no final testament, no will, and no legitimate heir—only an unacknowledged bastard daughter living incognito in the town of Streissen, whose existence every noble vying for the succession conveniently pretends not to know.
